title: Feelings and Value Judgments with Past Events

sections.content:
You know the subjunctive after feelings and value judgments (*me alegro de que…*, *es una lástima que…*) from A2 Unit 27. When the event has already happened, the feeling stays in the present and the verb becomes *haya* + participle:

• *Me alegro de que hayas venido.* (I am glad you came / have come.)
• *Siento mucho que no hayas aprobado el examen.* (I am sorry you didn't pass the exam.)
• *Es fantástico / una lástima que hayan tomado esa decisión.* (It is fantastic / a pity that they made that decision.)

sections.title: Rules and Patterns
rows: Me alegro de que hayas llamado.
Es una lástima que se haya roto.

items.spanish: Me parece maravilloso que hayan encontrado trabajo.
items.english: I find it wonderful that they have found work.

items.spanish: Siento que el concierto se haya cancelado por la lluvia.
items.english: I'm sorry the concert was cancelled because of the rain.

items.spanish: Es una pena que no nos hayamos visto antes.
items.english: It's a pity we haven't seen each other sooner.

sections.content: English often says 'glad you came' with the simple past. Spanish usually says *hayas venido*, because the feeling is felt now about an event that is finished.
